text: The X-ray confirms a bowel obstruction with no gas in the rectum. Given the age and "currant jelly" appearance of the stool often associated with this, does the baby pass any dark red or bloody stools, and is there a visible mass in the right lower quadrant of the abdomen? REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception.

The abdominal X-ray showing dilated bowel with no rectal gas, combined with the baby's severe tenderness and failure to pass stool, is highly suggestive of a bowel obstruction. Given the age and clinical presentation, this is most consistent with intussusception, which I suspect may be idiopathic rather than caused by an infection given the lack of fever or recent illness.
